description: SMA* (Simplified Memory-Bounded A*) runs A* on the search tree with at most `M` nodes in memory. When memory is full, it forgets the leaf with the largest `f`, and the parent remembers that child's value. The parent can then regenerate the child when it becomes the best part of the tree again. With an *admissible* heuristic (one that never overestimates), SMA* returns the cheapest path among those with at most `M − 1` edges. So it is optimal when some optimal path fits in memory. Use it when A* runs out of memory and IDA* repeats too much work.

papers.title: Efficient memory-bounded search methods
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 10th European Conference on Artificial Intelligence (ECAI)
